newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark says accepts EU shipyard subsidy ruling.
newsitem.headline: Denmark says accepts EU shipyard subsidy ruling.

text.p: Denmark's Trade Ministry on Wednesday said it accepted with reservations the European Commission's ruling that Danish A.P.Moeller's Odense Shipyard must repay excessive subsidy funds and would take immediate steps to refund the money to Brussels.

In a ministerial news release, Danish Trade Minister Jan Troejborg admitted that the EU and Denmark had divergent interpretations of the rules, with Brussels declining to accept that interest accrued on subsidy instalments could supplement subsidies.
"I disagree with the Commission on this point but take note of their assessment and will now contact Odense Shipyard with a view to getting the one million crowns refunded," said Troejborg.
The accounting practice was in line with ministerial shipbuilding subsidy regulations previously in force and Danish shipyards had acted in good faith, he added.
"The EU Commission's ruling makes it clear that Denmark has respected EU and OECD ship financing regulations (except for the one point)," Troejborg said.
A.P. Moeller said it had no further comment on the issue.
The European Commission ruled earlier that Odense Shipyard must repay around one million crowns in excessive state subsidies granted over five contracts in 1992.
The commission said in a statement that its decision was the result of a larger investigation into the financing of shipbuilding in Denmark during 1987-1993.
